# EDMeta: Exposure Distribution Meta-Regression Model

## Statistical Model

Let $i = 1, \ldots, n$ index studies. Each study reports an estimated effect $\hat{\beta}_i$ with standard error $\hat{\sigma}_i$, along with a summary of its study-specific exposure distribution on $[\text{l}_i, \text{u}_i]$.

$$\hat{\beta}_i | \beta_i \stackrel{\text{ind}}{\sim} \text{Normal}\left(\beta_i,\ \hat{\sigma}_i^2\right), \quad i = 1, \ldots, n;$$

$$\beta_i | \mu, \eta(\cdot), \tau^2 \stackrel{\text{ind}}{\sim} \text{Normal}\left(\mu + \int_{\text{l}_i}^{\text{u}_i} \eta(x)\, g_i(x)\, \text{d}x,\ \tau^2\right);$$

$$\int_{\text{l}_i}^{\text{u}_i} \eta(x)\, g_i(x)\, \text{d}x \approx \textbf{x}_i^{\text{T}} \left(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}(\rho)^{-1} \tilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}}\right);$$

$$\text{x}_{ij} = \frac{\text{u}_i - \text{l}_i}{m} \sum_{k=1}^{m} K(\text{d}_{ik}, \text{d}_j^*;\, \rho)\, g_i(\text{d}_{ik}), \quad j = 1, \ldots, m^*;$$

* $\beta_i$: latent true effect for study $i$;

* $\mu$: pooled mean effect;

* $\eta(\cdot)$: latent exposure-response function of primary interest;

* $\delta(x) = \mu + \eta(x)$: the exposure-response function reported in posterior inference;

* $\tau^2$: between-study variance;

* $g_i(\cdot)$: study-specific exposure density on $[\text{l}_i, \text{u}_i]$; either Uniform$(\text{l}_i, \text{u}_i)$ (`exposure_distribution = 0`) or Truncated Normal with mean `mid_exposure`$_i$ and standard deviation `sd_exposure`$_i$, truncated to $[\text{l}_i, \text{u}_i]$ (`exposure_distribution = 1`);

* $\text{d}_{i1}, \ldots, \text{d}_{im}$: equally-spaced midpoint quadrature points across $[\text{l}_i, \text{u}_i]$, with $\text{d}_{ik} = \text{l}_i + \left(k - \tfrac{1}{2}\right)\tfrac{\text{u}_i - \text{l}_i}{m}$;

* $\text{d}_1^*, \ldots, \text{d}_{m^*}^*$: equally-spaced knots spanning $[\text{l}^*, \text{u}^*]$, where $\text{l}^* = \min_i \text{l}_i$ and $\text{u}^* = \max_i \text{u}_i$;

* $K(x, x';\, \rho) = \exp\!\left\{-\rho\,\tfrac{|x - x'|}{\text{u}^*}\right\}$: exponential correlation function; $\rho > 0$ controls the rate of decay with exposure distance;

* $\textbf{x}_i = (\text{x}_{i1}, \ldots, \text{x}_{im^*})^{\text{T}}$: predictive process basis vector for study $i$;

* $\tilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}} = (\tilde{\eta}(\text{d}_1^*), \ldots, \tilde{\eta}(\text{d}_{m^*}^*))^{\text{T}}$: GP values at the knot locations;

* $[\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}(\rho)]_{jj'} = K(\text{d}_j^*, \text{d}_{j'}^*;\, \rho)$: $m^* \times m^*$ correlation matrix at the knots.

## Prior Information

$\mu \sim \text{Normal}(0,\ 100^2);$

$\tau^2 \sim \text{Inverse Gamma}(a_{\tau^2},\ b_{\tau^2});$

* Default setting: $a_{\tau^2} = 0.01$, $b_{\tau^2} = 0.01.$

$\tilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}} | \psi^2 \sim \text{Normal}\!\left(\mathbf{0}_{m^*},\ \psi^2\, \widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}(\rho)\right);$

$\psi^2 \sim \text{Inverse Gamma}(a_{\psi^2},\ b_{\psi^2});$

* Default setting: $a_{\psi^2} = 0.01$, $b_{\psi^2} = 0.01.$

$\rho \sim \text{Gamma}(a_\rho,\ b_\rho);$

* Default setting: $a_\rho = 1$, $b_\rho = 1.$

## Default Initial Values

* $\beta_i = \hat{\beta}_i$ for all $i$;

* $\mu = 0;$

* $\tilde{\boldsymbol{\eta}} = \mathbf{0}_{m^*};$

* $\tau^2 = 1.00;$

* $\psi^2 = 1.00;$

* $\rho = 1.00.$

## Metropolis Settings

* $\rho$ is updated via a Metropolis step on the log scale. The tuning parameter `metrop_sd_phi_eta_trans` controls the proposal standard deviation; target acceptance rate 20--40%.

## Approximation Settings

* `m_approx` ($m$): number of midpoint quadrature points per study used to approximate the integral over $g_i(\cdot)$. Default: 100.

* `m_star_approx` ($m^*$): number of predictive process knots spanning $[\text{l}^*, \text{u}^*]$. Default: 100.
